newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Products-Diffs near flat in torpid market.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Products-Diffs near flat in torpid market.

text.p: U.S. refined products differentials wiggled sideways Tuesday ahead of the weekly American Petroleum Institute inventory data, which showed supplies remained ample for the near-term.
On the NYMEX, July gasoline gained a modest 0.04 cent to settle at 55.68 cents a gallon and July heating oil slipped 0.35 cent to 51.57 cents a gallon.
U.S. GULF COAST
Distillate differentials were narrowly mixed, with activity viturally lifeless amid plentiful supply but a scarcity of buyers, traders said.
USG heating oil l Pipeline sold for 2.35 cents below July NYMEX futures, in line with Monday differentials, while prompt low sulfur diesel differentials eased a touch to 2.0 cents below the screen.

New API data for the week ending June 20 showed U.S. heating oil stocks growing by 2.0 million barrels and low sulfur diesel shrinking by 1.1 million barrels -- for a net distillate gain of 905,000 barrels.
"Obviously we're way oversupplied," one Gulf distillate player said, adding that increased supplies could only deepen bearish sentiment.
Prompt USG front-19th-cycle conventional unleaded "M1" gasoline, meanwhile, saw differentials ease about 0.15 cent from midday to about 3.25 cents below July futures.

Traders said API data showing a 592,000 barrel U.S. gasoline build -- including a 1.1 million barrel increase in the Gulf Coast -- were more likely to aggravate rather than cure the summer doldrums seen in recent weeks.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Reformulated gasoline differentials remained soft amid as record production and hefty imports created a steady stream of supply into the Harbor.
Reformulated gasoline was offered at 0.40 cent under NYMEX July gasoline while conventional unleaded differentials eased was offered at 3.00 cents under NYMEX.

Torrid refinery utilization rates have reflected breakneck gasoline output which reached a record 8.23 million barrels per day (bpd) the week before last. Moreover, imports have running above 400,000 barrels in recent weeks.
API data showed gasoline output for the week ended June 20 rose to 8.25 million barrels.
"The market well supplied and the prices reflect that. We are probably going to see more of the same story in the API stats tonight of high output and imports," said a Harbor dealer.
Prompt heating oil was mostly steady with Monday's levels, offered at 0.15 cent under the NYMEX contract.
MIDCONTINENT
Activity in the Midcontinent remained fairly subdued Tuesday, with few players actively seeking barrels, according to traders.
Prompt regular gasoline in Chicago was talked between about 1.00 and 1.25 cents over the July futures, slightly weaker than late Monday levels.

Group Three also saw only modest activity, though some firmness in the prompt gasoline was noted, with nearby barrels seen offered at about 5.25 cents over the July futures, up about 0.25 cent on the day.
However, low sulphur diesel in the Group dipped to between about 3.00 and 3.25 cents over the July NYMEX, down about 0.25 cent.
-- New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
